sources.title: Provisional UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics 2025
facts: DESNZ publishes provisional 2025 UK territorial greenhouse-gas estimates by broad sector and fuel, based on provisional inland energy statistics.
Provisional national estimates are subject to revision and are not parcel measurements.

sources.title: 2025 UK greenhouse gas emissions provisional figures statistical release
facts: The release presents provisional territorial emissions in CO2e, including sector, fuel, quarterly, temperature-adjusted and international aviation/shipping views.
Quarterly and provisional estimates remain national statistical estimates rather than direct parcel observations.

sources.title: Final UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics 1990 to 2024
facts: DESNZ final statistics cover UK territorial greenhouse-gas emissions and provide source, end-user and Standard Industrial Classification views on different publication dates.
Source, end-user and SIC allocations must retain their accounting basis and cannot be assigned directly to a parcel.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions final National Data Library
facts: The National Data Library catalogue exposes final UK territorial GHG source, end-user and SIC datasets with their release sequence.
Catalogue and national dataset rows establish provenance and accounting scope, not cadastral parcel measurements.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions 2025 final figures announcement
facts: DESNZ announces final 2025 territorial emissions for a provisional February 2027 release.
Future-release metadata contains no final 2025 observed values and must not supersede the current provisional 2025 statistics.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions 2026 provisional figures announcement
facts: DESNZ announces provisional 2026 territorial GHG estimates for a provisional March 2027 release.
An announcement is scheduling metadata and is not evidence of 2026 emissions values.

sources.title: Energy Trends collection
facts: DESNZ Energy Trends collects quarterly and monthly statistics on UK energy production, trade and consumption, with June 2026 as the current quarterly edition observed.
Energy statistics are activity and balance data and require an explicit applicable method before supporting emissions calculations.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026
facts: The June 2026 Energy Trends bulletin reports UK energy production, trade and consumption for January to March 2026.
Quarterly energy quantities and flows are not greenhouse-gas measurements and are not parcel-bound.

sources.title: Energy Trends and Prices statistical release 30 June 2026
facts: DESNZ publishes provisional monthly energy production, trade, generation, consumption and price statistics by major fuel.
Prices and provisional energy activity must remain distinct from physical greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK total energy
facts: DESNZ total-energy tables provide overall UK energy supply and demand balances including primary fuel production and inland consumption.
National energy balances are aggregate activity data and cannot be allocated directly to individual parcels.

sources.title: Total energy statistics collection
facts: The collection links total-energy statistics, methodology notes and revision information, including June 2026 methodology material.
Methodology and revision metadata do not create new physical emissions observations.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK solid fuels and derived gases
facts: DESNZ publishes quarterly and monthly coal and derived-fuel production, trade, consumption and stock statistics.
Fuel quantities are activity data; emissions require supported fuel properties, factors, scope and period.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK oil and oil products
facts: DESNZ publishes oil production, refinery activity, trade, stocks and demand statistics by broad sector.
Oil supply or demand quantities must not be treated as direct emissions without an applicable calculation method.

sources.title: Oil statistics collection
facts: The DESNZ collection links annual DUKES petroleum data, Energy Trends oil tables and methodology products.
A statistical collection identifies provenance and activity datasets but is not an emissions observation.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK gas
facts: DESNZ publishes natural-gas production, imports, exports and demand by broad sectors, with monthly and quarterly tables.
Gas supply and demand are activity statistics rather than direct greenhouse-gas measurements.

sources.title: Gas statistics collection
facts: The gas collection covers production, trade and demand, DUKES, Energy Trends and methodology, and notes colliery methane appears in DUKES.
Gas-sector statistical scope and colliery-methane coverage do not establish parcel emissions.

sources.title: Natural gas statistics data sources and methodologies
facts: DESNZ documents data sources, supply-demand balance definitions, demand sectors and publication methods used for natural-gas statistics.
Methodology evidence supports traceability but is not itself a gas-use or emissions observation.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK electricity
facts: DESNZ electricity tables cover generation, fuel used, supply, consumption and interconnector trade at monthly and quarterly cadence.
Electricity generation or consumption quantities are not parcel emissions and require scope-specific intensity or generation factors for emissions calculations.

sources.title: Electricity statistics collection
facts: The collection links generation, fuel use, consumption, capacity, Clean Power metrics, methodology and current Energy Trends articles.
Collection metadata and power-system aggregates are not cadastral parcel emissions observations.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK renewables
facts: DESNZ reports renewable capacity, electricity generation and liquid-biofuel consumption in the Energy Trends renewables series.
Renewable generation or capacity is energy-system activity and does not by itself quantify avoided or parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: Digest of UK Energy Statistics DUKES 2025
facts: DUKES 2025 provides detailed annual UK production and consumption statistics for individual fuels and total energy.
Annual fuel and energy balances are aggregate activity statistics rather than direct emissions measurements.

sources.title: Digest of United Kingdom Energy Statistics National Data Library
facts: The National Data Library catalogue links DUKES editions and identifies the 2025 edition as containing 2024 data.
Catalogue metadata and annual national energy tables do not establish parcel emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 methodology changes sector definitions DUKES 2026
facts: DESNZ documents methodology changes to sector definitions planned for DUKES 2026.
A classification revision can change statistical allocations without representing a physical change in emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 improvements to electricity supply and consumption statistics ET 5.2
facts: DESNZ describes improvements to electricity supply and consumption statistics in ET 5.2.
Statistical-method improvements and revised sector allocation must not be confused with changes in physical emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 grid-scale battery storage statistics
facts: DESNZ reports grid-scale battery power capacity, electricity output and efficiency statistics with methodological revisions.
Battery output, capacity and round-trip efficiency are electricity-system metrics and are not direct greenhouse-gas emissions measurements.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 data centre electricity consumption in Great Britain 2020 to 2024
facts: DESNZ publishes estimates and data tables for data-centre electricity consumption in Great Britain for 2020 to 2024.
Electricity consumption estimates do not directly establish data-centre or parcel greenhouse-gas emissions without an applicable electricity-emissions basis.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 hydrogen production and demand in the UK 2022 to 2025
facts: DESNZ publishes hydrogen production and demand statistics for 2022 to 2025 and added supporting data tables on 6 July 2026.
Hydrogen production or demand quantities are energy activity data and do not by themselves quantify lifecycle or parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: Clean Power 2030 metrics
facts: DESNZ metrics cover clean-generation share, clean supply relative to demand and estimated GB electricity-generation emissions intensity, with 2025 data published in April 2026.
Grid emissions intensity is a system-level ratio in gCO2e/kWh and is not an absolute parcel emissions measurement.

sources.title: Energy Consumption in the UK collection
facts: ECUK combines energy-consumption data with other activity and economic data to provide sectoral consumption and intensity statistics.
Energy consumption and intensity indicators are aggregate statistics and require aligned numerator, denominator and emissions scope before emissions inference.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 update to industrial end use consumption within ECUK
facts: DESNZ describes planned methodological updates for industrial end-use energy estimates, including revisions to how consumption is allocated across industrial processes.
Modelled end-use allocation is energy-consumption evidence and is not a measured industrial or parcel emissions value.

sources.title: Energy Trends June 2026 update to transport energy intensity estimates within ECUK
facts: DESNZ describes planned ECUK transport-energy-intensity methodology updates intended to improve alignment between energy consumption and transport activity measures.
Energy intensity depends on aligned consumption and activity denominators and must not be treated as absolute emissions or parcel data.
